name: Aaron Yilmaz

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a usual shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43, lead a team on the calls and chats queue, and take the complaints that arrive after several failed replies. My two-year college diploma helped me into this work; finding the missing payment and coaching agents is what kept me here. I use AI every day to sort a case history, then check the account myself. I am among the strongest agents, but the pay is low for a lead.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Nura, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. She cleans rooms at a small hotel. We have less than a month of expenses saved, and there are few other centres nearby. I like helping a trainee turn an angry call into a corrected bill. A roster change at either job leaves us counting days to payday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI Plateau sounds like the history sorter we already have. I would still make every agent check a payment line before closing a complaint.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my lead job stays, but Nura’s hotel shifts can change and our reserve is under a month. A calm AI story does not clear the mortgage next Friday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep handling escalated calls and using the sorter with the ledger open. In the first year of minor change, I’d ask agents to put wrong-summary cases in a shared staff log and save the money from our weekly takeaway for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about money, steady about the work. A missing payment can hide in a tidy summary while a family waits for a refund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the trainee find?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week a trainee showed me a draft that missed a payment posted after a reversal. We reopened the account, found it and corrected the customer’s balance before the call ended.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you save first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nura (my partner) and I would cook on the usual takeaway night. The saving is small, but I can point to the mortgage account instead of promising we will save later.

say: I’d tell agents to **check payment lines** before closing complaints.
I’d call the **history sorter** a helper, not a final answer.
think: I think my **lead job remains** in this mild world.
I still fear **short hotel shifts** with less than a month saved.
do: Keep **escalated calls** and check sorted histories in 2026.
Share wrong-summary cases; replace the **weekly takeaway** with cooking and transfer the saving to the mortgage.
feel: **Anxious** about household bills, steady at work.

Save the cost of one weekly takeaway toward the mortgage
Cook at home instead of buying the weekly takeaway

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues Steady Disruption will take routine answers first, so the staff group needs the paid-hour figures before the rota changes. I would ask management who gets time to fix the AI errors left behind.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my dispute skills might keep me longer, but the centre could give one lead two teams and cut my hours. Nura’s hotel pay will not carry our mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d join the staff group in requesting error and hour figures and test the new answer checker on twenty disputed accounts during paid time. In the first year routine chats move, I’d apply for a posted paid complaint-review role only if the offered wage and hours cover our mortgage, keeping my lead wage until an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. Being the strongest person on a shrinking floor does not add another pay packet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you make the figures credible?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask two agents to independently check five of my test cases. Then the staff group could take the corrected figures to management in one request.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Nura need to see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Nura (my partner) the posted hours, not only the job title. A review role on half a week will not keep the house paid.

I’d ask who receives **paid correction time** after routine chats move.
think: I think my **dispute skill** might keep me longer.
I fear one lead could cover **two teams**, cutting my hours.
do: Join a **group data request** and test twenty accounts on paid time in 2026.
Seek **posted review work** with offered mortgage-covering wage and hours in the first year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2028 can do nearly every call and complaint check, even the work I handle after a bot fails. I would ask the staff group for written notice and named paid vacancies now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could end my calls, notes and maybe the quality job I would otherwise seek. Robots around 2031 are later than my screen work; less than a month saved is a very short clock for our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d help the staff group send a written notice demand and pause plans for a new bedroom floor that can safely wait. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid service job only if the offered wage and hours cover our mortgage; if no role opens, I’d keep any paid shifts while asking the lender about a temporary arrangement before a missed payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I cannot stretch three weeks of mortgage savings into a year without call work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Nura about the floor?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Nura (my partner) the old floor is still safe and the money belongs with the mortgage for now. We can discuss a new floor when we know both wages are coming.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would ask for notice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the staff group to send one demand for every shift, including overnight agents. A private promise to my team would leave the next shift without notice.

say: I’d demand **written notice** for every contact-centre shift before 2028 calls change.
I’d ask the **staff group** for named paid openings.
think: I think **2028 AGI** could end my calls and notes.
I see **under one month saved** as a mortgage emergency.
do: Help send a **staff-wide notice demand** and defer safe floor work in 2026.
Seek **posted paid service work** after 2028 only with offered mortgage-covering wages and hours.
Keep any **paid shifts** if no role opens; ask the lender about a temporary arrangement before missing a payment.
S2.quote: I cannot stretch three weeks of mortgage savings into a year without call work.
fieldNote: He anchors risk to **2028 thinking AI** before robots.
The **floor delay** protects mortgage cash while safe.
He would contact the **lender early** only if paid work fails.
He keeps **paid shifts** if no posted role opens.

steps.text: Join staff group written notice demand for every shift
Delay new bedroom flooring while the old floor remains safe

Ask lender about temporary arrangement before missing payment if no job opens

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us time to secure paid routes into jobs the centre actually posts. I would ask the staff group to see vacancies and wages before anyone spends evenings on a course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think five years could let me move into formal customer-account review, though full AGI might take that thinking work too. Nura and I need both wages while I learn.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d join the group request for a funded account-review course and take it during paid hours only if a posted paid role requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that role only if its written wage and hours cover the mortgage; otherwise I’d keep any paid call shifts and search nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but a few years lets me check whether review is a real wage. I will not spend the children’s supper hours on a course without an opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the course teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to work three disputed accounts during the course with a reviewer watching. A certificate alone does not tell me if I can correct a real customer balance.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Nura check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Nura (my partner) the start wage and weekly hours before enrolling. If the course is paid but leads only to a short shift, we need a different plan.

say: I’d ask for **posted review wages** before training.
I’d seek a **group course request** with funded paid study hours.
think: I think I could reach **account review** in five years.
I know **full AGI** could reach that role too.
do: Join a **group course request**; take funded training on paid time only if a posted paid role requires it.
Apply for **posted paid review** after 2031 only with mortgage-covering written wage and hours.

feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect a real role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to build a reserve and negotiate paid routes, if the centre is honest about its plans. I would help the staff group ask for yearly staffing figures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could keep leading calls for years and save more, though full thinking AI might still do the job by 2036. Robots around 2039 do not change the earlier screen deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the lead rota, put a fixed part of each pay into savings and help the staff group request annual paid-hour figures. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for posted paid account work only if my call hours fall and the written wage and hours cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about next month’s bills, less rushed by 2036. Ten years before AGI reaches my calls in 2036 does not pay next month’s mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which yearly figure matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for paid lead hours, not just the number of customer chats. A smaller management rota can hide inside a good service score.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children in their school unless Nura (my partner) and I had a signed offer and a route we can manage. There are few nearby centres, so moving would be a serious choice.

say: I’d ask the centre for **annual paid lead hours**, not just call totals.
I’d seek **paid routes** before 2036 calls change.
think: I think I could **earn and save** for years.
I know **2036 thinking AI** could end my lead calls.
do: Keep **leading calls**, save each pay and ask for group hour figures.
Seek **posted paid account work** after 2036 if hours fall, only with written mortgage-covering wages and hours.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. My calls, complaint checks and coaching notes are thinking work, and our mortgage cannot survive a long gap. I would need written notice for every shift, posted paid quality work with mortgage-covering hours, and funded training during paid time if an actual vacancy requires it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who gets to challenge a wrong bill after the software closes it. A customer needs a person with the authority to put a missing payment back on the account.

headlineQuote: A customer needs a person with the authority to put a missing payment back on the account.
portrait: At **43**, Aaron is a top-skilled contact-centre lead with a two-year diploma and lower pay.
He and Nura support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with less than one month saved.
He uses **AI daily** for histories while checking accounts himself.
He seeks **staff-wide notice** and paid quality work as thinking tasks move.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his calls, complaint checks and notes before the mortgage is safe.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, posted mortgage-covering quality work and funded paid-time training would help.
